A placeholder disappears once someone types, and many readers treat it as pre-filled content. A persistent label tells people what each box wants.
Put a label element above the field, connected by for and id.
Use the placeholder as the only label.
Placeholder text has low default contrast and vanishes on input. It can show a format but never carry the instruction.
Keep placeholder for a short example and put rules in help text under the label.
Hide the required format in a placeholder.
A form error message in text, beside the field, names which field failed and why. A red border alone says something is wrong and nothing more.
Write an error message in text, adjacent to the field, naming the field.
Show a coloured outline or an icon only.
Enter an email like name@example.com
'Invalid input' is no help. Say what is expected, or offer the likely correction when it is known.
State the rule or the corrected value: what to type, not just what is wrong.
A screen reader only reads an error message beside a field if the two are linked. aria-describedby and aria-invalid connect them.
Set aria-invalid='true' and aria-describedby pointing at the message id.
Place the message in the DOM with no link to the input.
On a long form, errors below the fold go unseen. A summary at the top, moved to on submit, lists them with links to each field.
After a failed submit, focus a summary with links to every invalid field.
Reload the page with errors scattered and focus on nothing.
People need to know what they must fill in before they try. Choose one convention and explain it.
Use the required attribute, and say 'required' or '(optional)' in the label text.
Use a bare red asterisk with no key.
type=email, tel, url, number and date bring the right mobile keyboard and built-in checks. Wrong types make phone users hunt for the at sign.
Choose the input type that matches the data; add inputmode for numeric codes.
Autofill saves effort for people with motor or memory difficulties. The autocomplete attribute names the purpose so browsers can fill it.
Add autocomplete tokens such as given-name, email, street-address, postal-code.
Turn autocomplete off on name and address fields.
Within one process, asking for the same detail again, such as a billing address already given as delivery, costs time and errors.
Prefill from earlier steps or offer a 'same as' checkbox.
Make users retype details they just entered.
<label><input type='checkbox' checked> Billing same as delivery</label>
Logins must not depend on remembering or transcribing a code, or solving a puzzle, without an alternative such as paste, password manager or a link.
Allow paste, allow password managers, offer passkeys or email links.
Block paste in the password field or add a distorted-text puzzle.
Cancelling the paste event makes people retype long passwords and codes, and defeats password managers.
Leave paste enabled on every field, including confirm-email.
Cancel the paste event on any field.
Typing blind on a phone keyboard is the top cause of failed sign-ups. A show/hide control lets people check what they typed.
Add a toggle button with an accessible name and aria-pressed state.
Force a confirm-password field as the only check.
Validate on Blur, Not on Every Key
Showing 'invalid email' after the first letter is typed scolds people for being mid-sentence. Wait until they leave the field.
Validate on blur or submit; once a field is invalid, re-check as they type.
Flag errors while the user is still typing.
A message that stays after the field is corrected tells users it still fails, and a screen reader keeps announcing it.
Hide the message and drop the invalid flag the moment the value passes.
Wait for the next submit to clear it.
Keep Input After a Failed Submit
Wiping a long form because one field failed is the quickest way to lose a customer.
Re-render with the user's values and only mark the failing fields.
Reset the form or drop values on server error.
Do Not Disable Submit Up Front
A greyed-out button gives no clue why it is off and is skipped by keyboard users. Let them press and explain what is missing.
Keep the button enabled and show the error summary on submit.
Disable the button until every field looks valid.
Slow connections tempt people to press twice, creating duplicate orders. Show progress and ignore repeat presses.
Set aria-busy and a pending label on submit, and make the server idempotent.
Leave the button live while the request runs.
Navigating away from a half-filled form without warning throws away work. Ask first, or save drafts.
Listen for beforeunload only while the form is dirty.
Always show a leave prompt, even on clean forms.
People type phone numbers with spaces, dashes and brackets. Reject-on-format forces them to guess your rules.
Normalise on the server and accept spaces, case and common separators.
Return an error because of a space.
A set of radios or checkboxes needs a shared question. fieldset and legend give screen readers that context.
Wrap related choices in fieldset with a legend.
Put the question in a plain paragraph above the radios.
Review Before Legal or Money Commitments
Payments, bookings and legal submissions need a way to check, correct or reverse before the final commitment.
Show a review step with edit links and a clear final button that names the amount.
Charge on the same click that finishes the form.
Typing Japanese, Chinese or Korean uses a composition window where Enter confirms a character. Treating that Enter as submit sends half-typed text.
Ignore Enter while event.isComposing is true.
The right keyboard cuts typing time on phones. Numeric codes, email addresses and search each have one.
Set inputmode and enterkeyhint; use pattern for digit-only codes.
Show the full text keyboard for a six-digit code.
Image puzzles block blind users and many with cognitive disabilities. Prefer invisible checks, and give a non-puzzle path if one is needed.
Use server-side rate limits, honeypots or a challenge with an alternative.
Gate the form with a distorted-text puzzle.
Field Width Hints at the Answer
A postcode field as wide as the page suggests a paragraph. Width cues the expected length.
Size short fields (postcode, year, CVC) to fit their content.
Stretch every field to full width.
Choose Radios Over Selects for Few Options
With four or fewer options, radios show everything at a glance and take one click, where a select hides them behind two.
Use radios for up to about five choices and a select beyond that.
Hide three options in a dropdown.
